# Drafter notes — cid-tiradas-137-137c

21 units, 54 verses (3199–3249 incl. 3211b, wholly italic and unnumbered, and Pidal's own 3216b, 3236b), all
tirada 137, which ends here (tirada 138 begins at 3250, PDF p. 332).
`t` cut by script from packet.md (scratchpad b137c/build_137c.py reading b137c/units_src.py: each unit is given
as first/last verse id, and `t` = the packet lines joined by "\n", numbers stripped). The script asserts that every
packet verse is used once, in order (54); that each unit has 1–6 verses; that the `l` line count equals the `t`
line count; and that `i` is one paragraph. titleEn/part follow 137a/137b, with "third part" in `part`.

## Rubric
Rubric of 137 read on PDF 321 (printed 317). These clauses cover this section: "—Segunda demanda del Cid. El ajuar de sus
hijas. Los infantes hallan dificultad para el pago." The last word is damaged ("FAGO" at zoom 1) and read as
pago. Folded into the first note. Pidal's rubric calls the money el ajuar. The house term for axuvar is
"trousseau", and the poem says only averes, so the note states that this money is not the arras. Rubric of 138
(p. 332, "Acabada su demanda civil, el Cid propone el reto") is quoted in the last note as a pointer.

## Footnotes read on the scan (quoted exactly, with an English gloss)
PDF 329: 3204, 3205, 3211, 3213. PDF 330: 3215, 3216b, 3218, 3219, 3222, 3224, 3226, 3227. PDF 331: 3232, 3234,
3240, 3241. PDF 332: none before 3250 (3251 and 3256 belong to the next part). The note to 3216b points to the
note to v. 1922, which I read on PDF 254 (printed 250) and quoted, because it explains this si.
Paragraph indents seen at 3199, 3207, 3217, 3228, 3236 and 3241 are mentioned in the notes.

## Readings for the reviewer to check
1. **Footnote accents**: these were checked at zoom 4–5 and quoted as they appeared: exigía (3211), asistían, más (3215), así (3222),
   hacia and habia with no accent but transmitía with one (3232), más (3241). The accent on exigía is faint. Please confirm.
2. **3213 footnote headword "recudadas"**: Pidal prints this, against recudades in the text. I quoted it as printed and
   called it a slip.
3. **3226 footnote "juvizio"**: the italic z looks like s in this type (cf. Desid/desimos on p. 250). I quoted it as juvizio
   and the note says so.
4. **3240 footnote**: the first apreçiadura has the cedilla and the second "apreciaduras" has none. Both are quoted as printed.
5. **3211b**: wholly italic, unnumbered, so the letter b is ours (as with 3179b). Pidal gives no footnote. "do Remond" is
   kept as printed (do = don, cf. v. 3036).
6. **3204 dio = 'di yo'**: Pidal's note says this is first person. The `l`/`i` follow it ("I gave").
7. **3205 lo so**: "their own design" is our reading. What they "carried out" is left unsaid.
8. **3216b si**: following Pidal's notes to 3216b and 1922, this si heads a direct question ("will you give…?"). "if"
   is kept in `l`. "give an account of it" for dar razón is our rendering.
9. **3221 el que Valençia gañó**: the note says "perhaps scornfully", and this is our reading.
10. **3224 manfestados son**: Pidal glosses it 'cuando hubieron confesado'. The note says the subject is the Infantes. In `i`
    this is "had owned the debt".
11. **3227 dentro en la cort**: reading this as "then and there, not in lands at Carrión" is ours. Pidal's gloss
    is only 'paguen aquí'.
12. **3233 Tornárgelos quiero**: the brief lists this among the split futures. It is querer + infinitive with enclitics in
    split-future order, and the note says so.
13. **3235 non gelos quiero yo**: ge is read as 'from them' (the persons the marks would come from).
14. **3243 palafré de sazón**: "in prime condition, probably", as the glossary has it. The comma after sazón is damaged
    (establishment note).
15. **3246 Sobre**: rendered "over and above", following Pidal's note to 3232 ('descontando los 200 marcos').
16. **3248 enpréstanles**: we take the impersonal 3rd plural as "they borrow from others". This is a reading.
17. **3249 jogados**: there is no Pidal note on the page and no vocabulary to hand. "made fools of / made sport of" is our
    reading, marked uncertain. An alternative is "worsted, played out".
18. **Title "The Cid claims the dowry money"**: this is the given part name. Strictly, the money is the averes / Pidal's ajuar
    (trousseau) and not the arras (house "dower"). "Dowry" fits the bride's side in English, but the owner may prefer
    "the Cid claims his gift back" or similar.
19. **3229 Nos … la sabemos aquesta razón**: Nos is the royal "we". The doubled object is kept.
